source.title: How Truncating Weights Improves Reasoning in Language Models
source.authors: Lei Chen; Joan Bruna; A. Bietti

page_placements.theme: MLPs carry distributed context and competing associations

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates IOI behavior under low-rank MLP weight truncation, a different intervention from the original circuit’s head ablations and patching.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI predictions for GPT-2 Small and Pythia and measures how LASER weight truncation changes those predictions. It cites the original IOI circuit as prior work but does not test its head classes, circuit boundaries, or faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. It also reports unrelated reasoning and synthetic-task results, which are not included here.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It uses the IOI task only as a probe for MLP-stored generic-token associations. It applies LASER rank truncation to MLP weights and reports next-token probabilities of IO, S, 'the' and 'them'. It never identifies, ablates or patches the attention heads of the Wang et al. circuit, and never evaluates the circuit's faithfulness or completeness under any ablation, metric or prompt distribution. V5 concerns how faithful and complete the circuit looks under different evaluation choices. A whole-model MLP truncation that raises the IO-to-'the' ratio says nothing about that. The paper's link to the circuit is a citation: predicting [IO] 'requires a complicated architecture of attention heads' (Wang et al.). The MLP findings are real but measure a related construct, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that feed-forward layers learn simple distributional associations (e.g. 'to the') early in training, while attention carries in-context reasoning, with gradient noise as the theoretical explanation. Truncating selected MLP weights can therefore improve IOI, factual recall and few-shot GSM8K predictions. They draw no conclusions about the specific GPT-2 IOI circuit's heads or its evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LASER low-rank truncation of MLP weights and evaluates next-token predictions; it does not reproduce the original attention-head ablation, patching, or circuit-level criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: For GPT-2 Small, the reported decrease in “the” and “them” is described for MLP layers 9–11 and preserved-rank fractions ρ ∈ [0.1, 0.8]. The study also reports the IOI probability ratio at a Pythia-1B checkpoint after truncation.

fits_no_version.finding: Truncating late MLP input matrices lowers 'the'/'them' and raises the IO-to-'the' probability ratio. In GPT-2 small this holds for layers 9-11 on one prompt; in Pythia-1B the ratio goes from 2.3x to 12.3x at 14K steps. Pythia-410M and 1B final checkpoints show the same pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late MLP layers in GPT-2/Pythia carry distributional 'to the' associations that compete with the in-context IO prediction; low-rank truncation of them strengthens IO output.

fits_no_version.finding: Over Pythia-1B training, 'the' dominates from about 10 steps; [IO] is preferred over [S] and 'the' only after about 2000 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI ability emerges in training after generic bigram associations are learned.

fits_no_version.finding: In a synthetic noisy IOI task (App. J), dropping or truncating the last-layer MLP improves test accuracy for 3-7 layer transformers (SGD), and for L=3,4 with Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy transformers, final MLPs store generic noise associations that hurt IOI-like in-context prediction.

record.problems: The GPT-2 Small IOI demonstration uses one prompt. The rank-sweep probabilities in Figure 17 and the final-checkpoint probabilities in Figure 15 are figure-only in the text; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The experiments do not measure or ablate the proposed IOI head circuit.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant IOI results were left out. Other results in the paper concern synthetic noisy recall, factual recall, or GSM8K rather than the claim's IOI circuit versions.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, 7 classes, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not examined.
No name-mover ablation and no backup-head analysis.
IOI behaviour is shown in Pythia across checkpoints, but no head classes or roles are identified in any model.
No circuit faithfulness or completeness is computed under any ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
Only one prompt template (GPT-2) or one IOI dataset format (Pythia); no circuit analysis across prompt variants.

missing.what: Pythia-1B IOI training-dynamics phases (IO preferred after ~2000 steps)
Synthetic IOI task results with MLP dropping across 3-7 layers
Pythia-1B final-checkpoint IOI distribution under LASER

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 link is a stretch. V5 concerns the sensitivity of the circuit's faithfulness and completeness evaluation, and this paper never evaluates the circuit. The LASER layer and rho were chosen by searching for the best result, and GPT-2 results come from a single prompt. Relation 'discusses' reflects the motivating citation of Wang et al. only.

versions.untested_parts: The 26-head circuit, its seven classes and roles, and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria are not tested.
Backup heads and self-repair after main name-mover ablation are not tested.
The paper tests IOI predictions in more than one model, but does not test whether the same circuit classes and roles carry IOI, or whether components are reused for other tasks.
The paper does not compare circuit-finding methods, head-ablation types, or circuit evaluation metrics.

It tests MLP truncation settings and reports next-token probabilities, but does not compare circuit-ablation types or alternative evaluation metrics, vary IOI prompt formats, or quantify what fraction of behavior the proposed circuit explains.
The IOI tests use the reported prompt format; they do not compare name orders, templates, or examples with more names.

relation.reason: The paper discusses the prior attention-head circuit as an explanation for contextual predictions but does not test or operationally use that circuit.

tranche.reason: MLP truncation measures generic-token competition on IOI; it does not establish circuit head classes, backup mechanisms, circuit equivalence, or circuit evaluation sensitivity.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2, published at ICLR 2025, titled Distributional Associations vs In-Context Reasoning: A Study of Feed-forward and Attention Layers; the pack gives a different title. LASER layers, ranks and target weights were selected by search.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 Small layers 9–11 over ρ ∈ [0.1, 0.8], and Pythia-1B at 14K steps
reader_labels.reason: The reported effect on generic-token probabilities and the [IO]-to-“the” ratio varies with truncation settings and is consistent with evaluation sensitivity (r2-r7, r18).
